stem: Meera notes that the group of stars she sees from her Chennai terrace at 9 p.m. in January is different from the group she sees at 9 p.m. in July. Her teacher asks the class to explain why. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The stars move around the Earth once every 24 hours, so different stars appear.
Earth revolves around the Sun, so at the same time of night we face a different part of space at different times of the year.
Earth stops rotating on its axis for part of the year, so the sky changes.
The Sun moves to the other side of the sky at night, hiding some stars.

teacher.key_rationale: The yearly change in the night sky at a fixed time of night is caused by Earth's revolution around the Sun, not its daily rotation. Only option B states this correctly; A wrongly has stars orbiting Earth daily, C falsely claims rotation stops, and D wrongly moves the Sun across the night sky.
